Phoenix NWS discussion contains a convective/monsoon signal

afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 152321
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
420 PM MST Tue Sep 15 2026

.UPDATE...
Updated Aviation

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- The combination of abundant moisture and a weather system moving 
into the region will help to bring several rounds of showers and 
thunderstorms across south-central and eastern Arizona through 
Wednesday. 

- The main forecast concern will be heavy rainfall leading to flash 
flooding resulting in flood watches from late tonight through 
Wednesday evening across much of central and eastern Arizona. 

- Shower and thunderstorm chances will greatly diminish by Thursday, 
coming to an end starting Friday with the introduction of much drier 
air.  

- Near normal temperatures, briefly dropping to below normal levels 
across south-central AZ Wednesday, can be expected through the 
latter portion of the week before warming to slightly above normal 
levels by the weekend.

&&

.SHORT TERM /Today through Wednesday/...
A potentially very active period of weather is likely to 
materialize, especially late tonight through the day on Wednesday, 
across much of south-central AZ as several rounds of showers and 
thunderstorms with moderate to heavy rainfall leading to flash 
flooding are likely. Latest objective analysis shows the subtropical 
high centered over the southeastern states with an upper-level 
trough over the Pacific Northwest. This overall pattern 
configuration is resulting south to south-southwest over Arizona 
with more westerly flow from the lower Colorado River Valley 
westward through southern California, helping to bring in drier air 
across these areas. However, with the south to south-southwest 
situated across much AZ, it is continuing to bring a constant plume 
of subtropical moisture with PWATs across much of the south-central 
AZ lower deserts above 1.5". 

The combination of strong daytime heating and ample low-level 
moisture will drive MLCAPE values of 1000-1500 J/KG this afternoon 
with hi-res guidance indicating isolated to widely scattered storms 
developing across the higher terrain areas of eastern and 
southeastern AZ. Across the lower deserts of south-central AZ, there 
is also the potential of a few storms very late this afternoon 
through early this evening, especially across any terrain 
escarpments given the near zero convective inhibition that is 
forecast to be absent. Given the ample moisture in place, heavy 
rainfall leading to localized flooding will be the primary threat. 
However, strong downburst wind gusts will also be possible given 
that DCAPE values are still projected to be sufficient high, near 
1000 J/KG.

The main show is then forecast to materialize late tonight through 
Wednesday as moisture increases further along with the forcing for 
ascent. There will be a couple of features aloft that will provide 
the forcing with a mid-level shortwave over the southern Baja area 
expected to move overhead from the mid-morning to late afternoon 
hours on Wednesday along with an upper-level jet streak from the 
Pacific trough setting up along the Great Basin with the region 
expected to be located along the right entrance region, providing 
ample divergence aloft. The increased ascent combined with the ample 
moisture will result in widespread showers and thunderstorms, with 
the latest hi-res guidance indicating activity starting near to just 
after midnight with several rounds of activity into Wednesday 
evening. With projected PWATs expected to peak between 1.8-2.0" 
along with low-level mixing ratios as high as 14 g/kg and MUCAPE 
values in excess of 1000 J/KG, the overall environment will be 
favorable for thunderstorms to produce heavy rainfall rates in 
excess of 1-2"/hr and thus heighten the flash flood potential. Both 
the GEFS and EPS mean QPF show average amounts of 0.5-1.0" over the 
Phoenix area to over 1" over much of the higher terrain north and 
east of Phoenix. However, locally higher amounts are likely in the 
most persistent bands, with some of the HREF members showing amounts 
in excess of 3-4". Therefore, given the more widespread coverage 
along with the potentially very heavy rainfall amounts for portions 
of the area, a Flood Watch has been issued from late tonight through 
Wednesday evening for all of the south-central AZ lower deserts and 
the higher terrain areas east. Shower activity may persist across 
the region into the overnight period, however, activity should be 
lighter in nature given that most of the instability should be 
exhausted and the overall coverage will be diminishing as the upper-
level ascent shifts away.

Afternoon high temperatures today will generally be right around 
normal, with readings in the upper 90s to around 100 degrees across 
the south-central AZ lower deserts to lower 100s across the western 
deserts. With the abundant cloud cover and the rounds of rainfall 
activity forecast, much cooler temperatures are anticipated for 
Wednesday across south-central AZ with the potential that many areas 
struggle to hit 90 degrees for afternoon highs. Across the western 
deserts, afternoon temperatures with more sunshine should top out 
the upper 90s to low 100s. 

&&

.LONG TERM /Thursday through Monday/...
Drier air will gradually spread eastward on Thursday, with lower 
desert rain chances mostly coming to an end. However, lower level 
moisture will still remain in place likely allowing another round of 
showers and isolated thunderstorms on Thursday across the eastern 
Arizona high terrain. Given the drying aloft on Thursday, the threat 
for heavy rainfall is expected to be much lower than Wednesday. The 
synoptic flow is forecast to shift more out of the west northwest 
late this week into the weekend and this will help to bring a 
continuous flow of drier air through the region. By Friday, PoPs are 
at most 10-15% in eastern Gila County to near 0% in the Phoenix 
area. Lower level moisture should also eventually get scoured out 
with surface dew points dropping into the mid 30s to lower 40s 
across the western lower deserts to the upper 40s/lower 50s in the 
Phoenix area starting Saturday. 

Temperatures will mostly be an afterthought for the next several 
days with highs likely failing to reach 100 degrees in the Phoenix 
area through Thursday to right around normal for the western 
deserts. Once the drier air moves through the region later this 
week, temperatures will begin to warm with lower desert highs 
climbing up to around 105 degrees by Saturday.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 2320Z. 

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
Lower confidence forecast through Wednesday afternoon, however the 
threat exists of a longer duration, high impact TS event Wednesday 
morning into early afternoon. In the meantime, south winds may turn 
westerly mid evening, however confidence is low and a 150v240 type 
wind may prevail. The best odds are for SHRA/TSRA to remain just 
outside the KPHX airspace through the evening with less than a 20% 
chance of direct operational impacts before the overnight period. 
Trends in modeling suggests SHRA/TSRA not moving into the PHX area 
until after sunrise, though uncertainty on exact timing and location 
of TS impacts is high. 

At this time, will highlight the 15-19Z time frame as the most 
likely for significant operational impacts. In addition to direct 
TSRA sweeping through the PHX airspace, instances of MVFR (and 
possible brief IFR) flight categories are possible in the form of 
vsby and cigs. An initial period of strong wind gusts and BLDU is 
also possible, though precise details and chance of occurrence at any 
given terminal precludes inclusion in this TAF package. SHRA may 
linger well into the afternoon, and depending on the time of arrival 
of TSRA, a prolonged and more intense TS event may persist into the 
afternoon. The most likely outcome is for TS to leave the PHX area 
by mid afternoon with residual thick midlevel cigs and lack of 
instability for further development the remainder of the day. Should 
morning activity miss the PHX metro or fail to materialize, late 
afternoon and early evening SHRA/TSRA would become more likely. 


Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH: 
No weather issues will exist through Wednesday evening under mostly 
clear skies. Confidence is very good that KIPL winds will maintain a 
SE direction with periods of nearly calm conditions, while KBLH 
winds will continue southerly with afternoon gusts 20-25 kts.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Periods of scattered showers and thunderstorms are expected through 
Wednesday across the eastern districts supporting a heavy rainfall 
and flood threat. Moisture levels will remain elevated except for 
southeast California. Expect minimum humidity levels to still fall 
into a 15-25% range for the western districts while the eastern 
districts will only dip to 35-50% through Thursday. Winds will favor 
the south to southeast over much of the area through Wednesday with 
gusts of 20-30 mph at times across southwest Arizona. By Thursday 
into Friday, much drier air is forecast to spread eastward across 
the region, eventually ending rain chances for all but the far 
eastern Arizona high terrain along with lowering humidities.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...Flood Watch from midnight MST tonight through Wednesday evening 
     for AZZ534-537>563.

CA...None.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Lojero
LONG TERM...Kuhlman 
AVIATION...Ryan
FIRE WEATHER...Kuhlman/Lojero
